title: the DSG underground environment opener - the air supply duration, the fire and oxygen rules, the smoke system, the poisonous and noxious gases with the natural-gas explosion ladder and the small-bird warning, and the five-rung ventilation ladder

banner.title: The DSG UNDERGROUND ENVIRONMENT OPENER, R509: the printed pp. 36-37 (pdf 37-38) - the chapter opener (life underground shaped by the limits of sunlight and fresh air), the air supply duration (10 cubic feet per 24-hour rest, 12 moderate, 6 strenuous, the 2x/4x rates, the 3+4x5=23 example, the creature ratios, the post-exhaustion Con Check ladder with the -10 hp death floor and the 3-per-turn recovery), fire and oxygen (the small-fire 10-foot cube in 2 hours, torch 8 hours, the 4x scaling, the oil 3-rounds-as-turns rule), the smoke system (the 1-foot layer per turn per 10x10, ceiling stacking, the Con Check with 1d6 damage and 1d6 recovery, the cumulative rule and the 33-28-5 orc death example), the poisonous and noxious gases (save vs. poison vs. the -3/-3 Con Check economy, the natural-gas 20% explosion ladder with its Wisdom Check, the small-bird early warning) and the five-rung ventilation ladder
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read - every numeric cell dual-confirmed; the garble classes settled: djvu "213 as much oxygen" = 2/3 (Acrobat "consumes 2/3 as much"), the percent-glyph garbles (1096/496-class) = 10% and +4%-style, Acrobat "112" = 1/2 (the halved rates), Acrobat "ld6/ld4" = 1d6/1d4. Odor detection (pp. 37-38) and its Tables 15-16 begin the NEXT round - this slice ends at the sealed-rung ladder.
banner.sentinel: Pure prose round - no printed grid, no tables, no sentinels. The ventilation pins are the ENVIRONMENTAL-scale ladder; the R508 dnrVent pins are the Battlesystem-scale modifiers - related seams, nothing auto-credited either way. The breath-holding scope note pins as a bool with the WSG R454 cross-reference in its comment.

audit_comment: The DSG underground environment opener pins the air supply duration (10 cubic feet per human per 24 hours at rest, 12 hours moderate, 6 hours strenuous, the 2x and 4x consumption rates, the 3-hours-rest-plus-4-times-5 example at 23 hours, the creature ratios at 2/3, 1/2 and 2x, the post-exhaustion Con Check ladder - each failure draining 1 from every ability and 1 hit point, further checks against the reduced Con, unconscious at all-zero abilities, dead at -10 hit points, automatic once Con hits 0, the immediate 3-per-turn recovery on fresh air, and the air-only scope that excludes breath-holding), the fire and oxygen rules (the 1-foot small fire draining a 10-foot cube in 2 hours/12 turns, the torch at 8 hours, the small-fire-equivalent scaling at 4x, the 3-round oil flask counted as 3 turns), the smoke system (the 1-foot layer per turn per 10-by-10 area stacking from the ceiling until floor-liers are affected, wet or green fuel and fabric and oil as the smoke sources, the per-round Con Check with 1d6 damage, the 1d6-per-round fresh-air recovery, the cumulative rule, the 33-hit-point character losing 28 and dying to the orc's 5-point blow), the gases (poisonous gases saving vs. poison, noxious gases Con Checking every round for -3 abilities and -3 attacks with no hit-point loss and 3 per turn recovery, the gas-replaces-oxygen fold into the air system, the natural-gas 20-percent-per-round explosion at 1d6 with a 1d6 damage and 1 Wisdom step per 10 percent potency, no Wisdom Check for odorless gas, and the secret small-bird save one turn early as a 0th-level human against gradually increasing gas) and the five-rung ventilation ladder (well-ventilated, subtle, connected, none and sealed with their smoke, gas, spell and oxygen clauses).

consts.name: dnaAirRestCubicFeet
consts.comment: a human-sized creature at complete rest depletes the oxygen in 10 cubic feet of air.

consts.name: dnaAirRestHours
consts.comment: the same 10 cubic feet lasts 24 hours at complete rest.

consts.name: dnaAirModerateHours
consts.comment: even moderate physical activity halves the air supply to 12 hours.

consts.name: dnaAirStrenuousHours
consts.comment: strenuous exertion cuts the air supply to a mere 6 hours.

consts.name: dnaAirModerateRateMult
consts.comment: a moderately exercising character uses oxygen twice as fast as one at rest.

consts.name: dnaAirStrenuousRateMult
consts.comment: a character working strenuously uses oxygen four times faster than a resting one.

consts.name: dnaAirExampleRestHours
consts.comment: the worked example: the character rests for 3 hours.

consts.name: dnaAirExampleWorkHours
consts.comment: the worked example: then works hard for 5 hours.

consts.name: dnaAirExampleTotalRestHours
consts.comment: the worked example total: 3 hours of rest plus 4 times 5 hours of work equals 23 hours of resting-rate oxygen.

consts.name: dnaAirDwarfElfNum
consts.comment: a dwarf or elf consumes oxygen at two-thirds the human rate: the numerator.

consts.name: dnaAirDwarfElfDen
consts.comment: a dwarf or elf consumes oxygen at two-thirds the human rate: the denominator.

consts.name: dnaAirHalflingDogDen
consts.comment: a halfling or a dog uses only half as much oxygen as a human.

consts.name: dnaAirMuleOgreMult
consts.comment: a mule or an ogre consumes oxygen at twice the human rate.

consts.name: dnaAirFailAbilityLoss
consts.comment: every failed post-exhaustion check reduces each ability score by 1.

consts.name: dnaAirFailHpLoss
consts.comment: every failed post-exhaustion check also reduces the hit point total by 1.

consts.name: dnaAirDeathHpFloor
consts.comment: when the hit point total reaches -10, the character is dead.

consts.name: dnaAirRecoverPerTurn
consts.comment: on recovery, hit points and ability scores all climb at 3 points per turn until original levels.

consts.name: dnaFireSmallMaxDiameterFeet
consts.comment: a small fire is one foot or less in diameter.

consts.name: dnaFireSmallCubeFeet
consts.comment: a small fire consumes all of the oxygen in a ten-foot cubic space.

consts.name: dnaFireSmallHours
consts.comment: the small fire exhausts that ten-foot cube of oxygen in 2 hours.

consts.name: dnaFireSmallTurns
consts.comment: the same consumption expressed in turns: 12 turns.

consts.name: dnaFireTorchHours
consts.comment: a flaming torch consumes all of the oxygen in the same ten-foot cube in 8 hours.

consts.name: dnaFireScaleExampleMult
consts.comment: a fire four times larger than a small fire consumes oxygen four times as fast.

consts.name: dnaOilBurnRounds
consts.comment: oil in a flask or similar small container burns for 3 rounds.

consts.name: dnaSmokeLayerFeet
consts.comment: a small fire produces enough smoke in one turn to create a one-foot-thick smoke layer.

consts.name: dnaSmokeAreaFeet
consts.comment: that smoke layer covers a 10-foot by 10-foot square area.

consts.name: dnaSmokeScaleExampleMult
consts.comment: the smoke example multiplier: 3 times the fire, 3 times the smoke rate.

consts.name: dnaSmokeDamageDie
consts.comment: a failed smoke check means the character suffers 1d6 hit points of smoke damage.

consts.name: dnaSmokeRecoverDie
consts.comment: the smoke-damage recovery die: 1d6 points per successful fresh-air round.

consts.name: dnaSmokeExampleCharHp
consts.comment: the smoke example character has 33 hit points.

consts.name: dnaSmokeExampleLoss
consts.comment: he loses 28 of them to smoke inhalation.

consts.name: dnaSmokeExampleOrcHit
consts.comment: an orc strikes him for 5 points of damage before he regains any smoke losses - the 5 remaining points mean he is killed.

consts.name: dnaNoxiousAbilityLoss
consts.comment: a failed noxious-gas check results in a general lowering of ability scores by 3.

consts.name: dnaNoxiousAttackPenalty
consts.comment: the same 3-point penalty is applied to attack rolls (the modern example: tear gas).

consts.name: dnaNoxiousRecoverPerTurn
consts.comment: ability scores are raised at 3 per turn once the character can breathe fresh air again.

consts.name: dnaNatGasExplodePct
consts.comment: the base chance of a natural-gas explosion is 20 percent per round.

consts.name: dnaNatGasDamageDie
consts.comment: the explosion causes 1d6 points of damage to all characters and creatures in the area with the gas.

consts.name: dnaNatGasPotencyStepPct
consts.comment: the potency step: each 10 percent increase in the chance of explosion.

consts.name: dnaNatGasPotencyDieStep
consts.comment: each potency step adds another 1d6 to the damage inflicted.

consts.name: dnaNatGasWisBonusPerStep
consts.comment: higher concentrations add 1 to the characters' Wisdom scores per potency step, for purposes of this Wisdom Check only.

consts.name: dnaBirdSaveLevel
consts.comment: the bird saves as a 0th-level human.

consts.name: dnaVentWellGasTurns
consts.comment: poisonous or noxious gases remain in a well-ventilated area for 2 turns unless more gas is introduced.

consts.name: dnaVentSubtleGasHours
consts.comment: in a subtly ventilated area, poisonous or noxious gases remain effective for 1 hour.

consts.name: dnaVentSubtleLargeSmokeDiv
consts.comment: smoke from large fires or burning oil accumulates at half the rate listed for enclosed areas in a subtly ventilated area.

consts.name: dnaVentConnectedSmallSmokeDiv
consts.comment: an area with no visible ventilation but connected to ventilated areas or the surface collects small-fire smoke at half the rate.

consts.name: dnaVentConnectedGasMinHours
consts.comment: poisonous or noxious gases remain in a connected area for 2-5 hours (1d4+1): the minimum.

consts.name: dnaVentConnectedGasMaxHours
consts.comment: the 2-5 hour connected-area gas duration: the maximum.

consts.name: dnaVentNoneGasHours
consts.comment: poisonous or noxious gases remain in an unventilated area for a full 24 hours.

consts.name: dnaSealedSmokeLingerDie
consts.comment: smoke that collects in a sealed room lingers for 1d6 hours after the fire that created it goes out.

bools.name: dnaAirDmAppliesToCreatures
bools.comment: the DM applies the oxygen ratio to all characters and to any creatures, such as mules or dogs, that accompany them.

bools.name: dnaAirConCheckEachTurnAfterExhaust
bools.comment: each turn after the oxygen is exhausted, the character must make a Constitution Check.

bools.name: dnaAirCheckAgainstReducedCon
bools.comment: each additional Constitution Check is made against the reduced Constitution score - the character grows more feeble as he gulps the last oxygen.

bools.name: dnaAirUnconsciousAtZeroAbilities
bools.comment: when all ability scores have dropped to 0, the character is unconscious.

bools.name: dnaAirAutoDeathAtConZero
bools.comment: death becomes automatic once the Constitution score reaches 0, since all further Constitution Checks automatically fail.

bools.name: dnaAirRecoveryImmediateOnFreshAir
bools.comment: if fresh air is introduced before death, the character begins to recover immediately.

bools.name: dnaAirOnlyInAirNotBreathHolding
bools.comment: this system is used only for characters in an area with air - it cannot be used for characters holding their breath (the WSG breath-holding pins are a separate system; nothing auto-credited).

bools.name: dnaAirCaveInCutsVentilation
bools.comment: if a cave-in occurs, ventilation sources may be cut off - the potential for air supply problems should not be overlooked.

bools.name: dnaAirCrowdingOutpacesVentilation
bools.comment: a chamber may be so crowded that a meager ventilation system cannot replace oxygen as fast as it is depleted.

bools.name: dnaFireScalesBySmallFireEquivalents
bools.comment: the oxygen consumption of larger fires is based on the number of small fires they equal.

bools.name: dnaFireGoesOutWithoutOxygen
bools.comment: when all of the oxygen is consumed, the fire goes out.

bools.name: dnaOilRoundCountsAsTurn
bools.comment: for oxygen consumption, burning oil is treated as a small fire and each round of burning counts as a full turn - 3 rounds use the oxygen of 3 turns of wood fire.

bools.name: dnaSmokeFromWetOrGreenFuel
bools.comment: if any of the fuel is wet, or if green or living branches, twigs or leaves are used, smoke is produced.

bools.name: dnaSmokeFromFabricAndOil
bools.comment: any kind of burning fabric creates smoke, as does burning oil.

bools.name: dnaSmokeLayersStackFromCeiling
bools.comment: the smoke rises and collects against the ceiling; each next turn of smoke collects below the previous layer until the breathable air is concentrated near the floor.

bools.name: dnaSmokeFillsRoomAffectsFloor
bools.comment: finally the entire room fills with smoke and even characters lying on the floor are affected.

bools.name: dnaOilSmokeRateByRound
bools.comment: an oil fire creates the same amount of smoke as an average fire, except that the rate is calculated by round instead of by turn.

bools.name: dnaSmokeScalesWithFireSize
bools.comment: a fire three times as big as a one-foot-diameter fire creates smoke three times as fast.

bools.name: dnaSmokeConCheckEachRound
bools.comment: a character forced to breathe smoke must make a Constitution Check each round that the smoke is inhaled.

bools.name: dnaSmokeDamageTemporary
bools.comment: smoke damage is temporary - with a chance to breathe fresh air the character makes a Constitution Check every round, regaining 1d6 points on a success.

bools.name: dnaSmokeDamageCumulative
bools.comment: smoke damage is real: any other damage taken while a character suffers from smoke damage must be considered cumulative with it.

bools.name: dnaGasPoisonSaveVsPoison
bools.comment: poisonous gases generally require characters to make saving throws vs. poison.

bools.name: dnaGasOxygenReplacementTreatedAsExhaustion
bools.comment: any gas - poisonous, noxious, or harmless - can replace the oxygen in an area; the effects are treated as the air-supply exhaustion explained earlier.

bools.name: dnaNoxiousConCheckEachRound
bools.comment: noxious gases force characters to make Constitution Checks every round.

bools.name: dnaNoxiousHelplessAtZeroAbilities
bools.comment: characters can be rendered quite helpless by noxious gases when all ability scores are reduced to 0.

bools.name: dnaNoxiousNoHpLoss
bools.comment: but they are not killed - noxious gases cause no loss of hit points.

bools.name: dnaGasDmAdjustmentsAllowed
bools.comment: modifiers to the saving throw or Constitution Check can be applied as the DM sees fit, for exceptionally lethal or mild poisons or degrees of noxiousness.

bools.name: dnaOdorlessGasNoWisCheck
bools.comment: if a gas is completely odor-free, no Wisdom Check should be allowed - the check represents awareness of the odor.

bools.name: dnaStrongOdorAllowsBreathHold
bools.comment: strong-odor gases such as sulphur give the characters a chance to hold their breath before the full force of the gas takes effect.

bools.name: dnaNatGasExplodesWithOpenFlame
bools.comment: natural gas with a torch, candle, lantern or any other open flame has a chance per round of exploding.

bools.name: dnaNatGasWisCheckOnlyIfCareful
bools.comment: characters entering natural gas might be allowed Wisdom Checks only if they are moving slowly and investigating their surroundings carefully.

bools.name: dnaBirdWarnsOneTurnEarly
bools.comment: a small bird with the party gives early warning of gradually increasing poisonous gas: the bird's save comes one turn before the characters must save.

bools.name: dnaBirdSaveSecret
bools.comment: the DM should make a secret saving throw vs. poison for the bird.

bools.name: dnaBirdDiesOnFailedSave
bools.comment: if the bird's saving throw fails, the bird dies.

bools.name: dnaBirdOnlyGradualGas
bools.comment: the bird warning is of little help if gas is suddenly introduced in high concentration - only a gradually increasing amount gives any early warning.

bools.name: dnaVentWellNoSmokeAccumulation
bools.comment: in a well-ventilated area (a noticeable airflow), smoke does not accumulate.

bools.name: dnaVentWellNoOxygenExhaustion
bools.comment: nor is the oxygen exhausted by characters breathing or by fire in a well-ventilated area.

bools.name: dnaVentWellGasSpellsHalved
bools.comment: the duration of all gas-based spells is halved in a well-ventilated area.

bools.name: dnaVentSubtleSpellsNormal
bools.comment: with subtle air movement (detected by the flickering of a torch or candle), gas-based spells linger for their normal durations and fresh air is not a problem.

bools.name: dnaVentSubtleSmallSmokeNoAccumulation
bools.comment: smoke from small fires or torches does not accumulate in a subtly ventilated area.

bools.name: dnaVentConnectedLargeSmokeNormal
bools.comment: large or oil fires fill such a connected area with smoke at the usual rate.

bools.name: dnaVentConnectedBreathNeverExhausts
bools.comment: characters do not use up all the air through breathing in a connected area - even minimal ventilation allows enough air movement for respiration.

bools.name: dnaVentConnectedSpellsNormal
bools.comment: the duration of all gas-based spells is normal in a connected area.

bools.name: dnaVentNoneSmallSmokeNormal
bools.comment: an area with no noticeable ventilation and no outflow captures smoke at the normal rate, even from small fires.

bools.name: dnaVentNoneHeavierThanAirException
bools.comment: the 24-hour figure holds unless the gas is specifically noted as heavier than air.

bools.name: dnaSealedAirFinite
bools.comment: an area completely sealed off (by cave-ins, mortared stone walls, or walls of force) has a finite air supply that once used up can only be replaced by introduced fresh air.

bools.name: dnaSealedEffectsNormalRates
bools.comment: in a sealed area all of the effects apply at their normal rates of accumulation and effect.

bools.name: dnaSealedGasUntilVented
bools.comment: poisonous or noxious gases remain in a sealed area until vented out by the admission of fresh air.

bools.name: dnaSealedSpellsNormal
bools.comment: the duration of all gas-based spells is normal in a sealed area.
